proof:
The lattice census is the $n=2$ case of 11ed3ca552482ee9. All four fibers are $K$, and their pooled within-fiber covariance equals $\Sigma$. Each affine barycentric permutation preserves uniform probability on $K$, so its linear part preserves the covariance norm on covectors under pullback. It also preserves $f$. The three cyclic permutations average every point of $K$ to $g$. Concavity gives $f(g)\ge f(x)$ for all $x$, and equality for $x\ne g$ would force $f$ to be constant on $[g,x]$, contradicting strict interior concavity. Invariance under the cyclic permutation forces the derivative at its fixed point $g$ to be zero: on covectors the sum of the three pullbacks is zero, because the sum of their centered actions on vectors is zero.

For the own infimum normalize to $\Gamma(u)=1$. This is a compact ellipse, and continuity of the integrated kernel gives an attained own minimum. Uniformly over that ellipse, the smoothed capture at $g$ differs from ordinary capture by at most the volume in the band $|u\cdot(X-g)|\le\epsilon f(g)+h$. Its volume tends to zero uniformly by the parallel-section bound of the fixed triangle and the uniform positive lower bound on $\lVert u\rVert$. A through-centroid one-vertex cap has edge intercept ratios $\alpha,\beta\in(0,1]$ measured from its captured vertex, with $\alpha^{-1}+\beta^{-1}=3$. Its area fraction is $\alpha\beta\in[4/9,1/2]$, with minimum only at $\alpha=\beta=2/3$. The complementary two-vertex orientation has area at least $1/2$, and the cuts through a vertex are included as endpoint cases. This proves that the ordinary minimum is $4V/9$ and has exactly the three canonical vertex orientations. Hence $q_{\epsilon,h}\to4V/9$ and is less than $V$ for small parameters. Every smoothed minimizing direction at $g$ approaches the three canonical orientations as the parameters tend to zero, by uniform convergence on the compact ellipse and continuity of the ordinary cap mass.

Take any minimizing normalized direction at $g$ and its cyclic pullback orbit $u_0,u_1,u_2$. All are minimizing, they are distinct and sum to zero. A repeated element would make the first direction a nonzero fixed covector, which is impossible because the sum of the three pullbacks is zero. For $x\ne g$ choose an orbit direction with $u_j\cdot(x-g)\ge0$. For this direction the own margin at $x$ is the own margin at $g$ shifted by the strictly negative constant $-u_j\cdot(x-g)+\epsilon(f(x)-f(g))$. For all normalized directions the positive and negative support distances from $g$ have positive uniform lower bounds, since $g$ has an interior ball. Thus for small $\epsilon,h$ the strip at $g$ given by $-h<u_j\cdot(X-g)+\epsilon f(g)<0$ lies between proper parallel cuts and has positive area. The integrated ramp is nondecreasing in the additive margin offset, with derivative equal to strip area divided by $h$, which is positive near its offset at $g$. The derivative follows by differentiating the ramp away from the two strip boundaries, which are area null. Any strictly negative shift decreases the capture, so $\theta_{\epsilon,h}(x)<q_{\epsilon,h}$. This includes boundary marks.

For any oblique cap through $(0,g)$, take one uniform point $X$ of $K$ and assign its three cyclic permutations $X_j$ to the three outer fibers. They are each uniform and $\sum_jX_j=3g$. Since $\sum_jv_j=0$, the sum of the three unscaled margins is $3\epsilon f(g)\Gamma(u)>0$. At least one margin is nonnegative for each $X$, so the total outer capture is at least $V$. The own capture is at least $q_{\epsilon,h}$. For any chosen own minimizing direction a finite exposing tilt can saturate the kernel at one on one prescribed outer fiber and at zero on the others while leaving the own term unchanged. Indeed the base forms
$$
\ell_0(z)=-z_1-z_2,\qquad \ell_1(z)=3z_1-z_1-z_2,\qquad \ell_2(z)=3z_2-z_1-z_2
$$
take value $2$ at their matched vertex and $-1$ at the other two, and the continuous margins are uniformly bounded on the normalized ellipse. A sufficiently large common multiplier of these forms gives the claimed saturation. A closed pure-base cap through zero contains the entire middle fiber and at least one outer fiber, so its mass is at least $2V>V+q_{\epsilon,h}$. The mixed depth at $(0,g)$ is therefore exactly $V+q_{\epsilon,h}$.

At any $(0,x)$ the same tilt construction with an own minimizing direction gives mixed depth at most $V+\theta_{\epsilon,h}(x)$. At $(v_j,x)$ the own term gives a lower bound $\theta_{\epsilon,h}(x)$ for every cap, including pure-base caps. Since $v_j$ is strictly exposed, a large finite base tilt of an own minimizing oblique cap excludes all other fibers and attains that lower bound. Together with strict own uniqueness this proves the global claim.

For the menu use the three normalized cyclic own directions with the three matching exposing tilts. They all minimize at $(0,g)$. Their strips occur only on the middle fiber, so their strip base centroids are zero, and cyclic symmetry gives equal positive threshold coareas $S_j$. The positive weights $\rho_j=1/3$ satisfy the continuous balance, and the response weights proportional to $\rho_j/S_j$ are also $1/3$. The cyclic pullback construction gives the stated own profiles.

statement:
Let $B=\operatorname{conv}\{v_0=(-1,-1),v_1=(1,0),v_2=(0,1)\}$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a triangle of area $V>0$ and centroid $g$. The actual positive-volume lattice fibers of $B\times K$ are the four copies of $K$ at $z=0,v_0,v_1,v_2$. Let $f:K\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous and concave, strictly concave in $\operatorname{int}K$, differentiable and positive near $g$, and invariant under affine barycentric permutations. Use it at each of the four bases. Let $\Gamma(u)=(u^\mathsf T\Sigma u)^{1/2}$ for the covariance $\Sigma$ of uniform probability on $K$, and let $\Psi(t)=\min(1,\max(0,1+t))$. At a mark $(p,x)$, an oblique cap $(a,u)$ with $u\ne0$ has mixed capture
$$
\sum_{z\in B\cap\mathbb Z^2}\int_K\Psi\left(\frac{a\cdot(z-p)+u\cdot(X-x)+\epsilon f(x)\Gamma(u)}{h\Gamma(u)}\right)dX .
$$
Define its mixed depth as the infimum over these caps and the ordinary closed pure-base caps through $p$. Write $\theta_{\epsilon,h}(x)$ for the infimum over $u\ne0$ of the one-fiber term at $p$ and $q_{\epsilon,h}=\theta_{\epsilon,h}(g)$.

For all sufficiently small $\epsilon,h>0$, $g$ uniquely maximizes $\theta_{\epsilon,h}$, and $(0,g)$ is the unique mixed deepest mark, of raw depth $V+q_{\epsilon,h}$, where $q_{\epsilon,h}\to4V/9$ as $(\epsilon,h)\to(0,0)$. At each exposed outer base $v_j$, the pointwise mixed depth is $\theta_{\epsilon,h}$. At $(0,g)$ there is a three-cap menu of minimizing directions $u_j$ with $\Gamma(u_j)=1$, equal positive threshold coareas, continuous balance $\sum_j u_j/3=\epsilon\nabla f(g)=0$, equal response weights $1/3$, and strip base centroid zero for every cap. Cap $j$ is saturated at one on the matched fiber $v_j$ and zero on the other outer fibers. Its own profile is the cyclic barycentric image of the first cap's own profile.
title: An actual positive-width triangle-product singleton and a balanced minimizing menu
